subtitle: b. 1944, Surakarta, Central Java — Founder of PAN, Architect of the Central Axis & Speaker of the MPR (1999–2004)
desc:
Born in Surakarta (Solo), Central Java, in 1944 into a devout modernist Muslim family, Muhammad Amien Rais earned a political science doctorate from the University of Chicago before teaching at Gadjah Mada University in Yogyakarta. Briefly an early member of Habibie's ICMI think tank, he was forced out after criticizing foreign mining contracts at Freeport and Busang, and in 1995 became Chairman of Muhammadiyah, Indonesia's second-largest Islamic organization. In early 1998, as the rupiah collapsed, he emerged as the most fearless national figure demanding Suharto's resignation and calling for a total campaign against Korupsi, Kolusi, dan Nepotisme (KKN).

Expecting his prominence in the May 1998 uprising to translate into sweeping electoral support, Amien founded the pluralist National Mandate Party (PAN) in August 1998, but finished a disappointing fifth in the June 1999 election with just 7.1% of the vote and 34 DPR seats. Refusing to be sidelined, he engineered the Poros Tengah (Central Axis)—a loose alliance of modernist and traditionalist Islamic parties—to block both a second term for Habibie and a presidency for secular-nationalist frontrunner Megawati Sukarnoputri. By cutting deals with Akbar Tandjung's Golkar faction and General Wiranto in early October 1999, Amien won election as Speaker of the MPR, presiding over the rejection of Habibie's Accountability Speech and the surprise election of Gus Dur.

Less than two years after installing Gus Dur in the palace, Amien turned against him and spearheaded the July 2001 MPR Special Session that removed Gus Dur and elevated Megawati. As MPR Speaker through 2004, he oversaw the four historic constitutional amendments that stripped the MPR of its presidential-selection powers and established direct presidential elections. After finishing fourth in the 2004 presidential race, he remained an outspoken political gadfly, breaking with PAN in 2020 following internal leadership disputes to found the minor Ummat Party.

subtitle: b. 1945, Sibolga, North Sumatra — Chairman of the Golkar Party (1998–2004) & Speaker of the DPR (1999–2004)
desc:
Born in Sibolga, North Sumatra, in 1945, Akbar Tandjung rose through the Muslim Students' Association (HMI) in Jakarta during the 1966 student demonstrations that helped bring Suharto to power. A patient party organizer and veteran of three consecutive Suharto cabinets (serving as Minister of Youth and Sports and Minister of Public Housing), he served as President Habibie's Minister/State Secretary while winning a fierce battle against retired Gen. Edi Sudradjat at Golkar's July 1998 Extraordinary Congress to become Chairman of the newly reorganized Golkar Party.

Tasked with salvaging the New Order's hated electoral machine, Akbar kept Golkar alive in the June 1999 election, securing second place with 22.4% of the vote (120 DPR seats). Behind the scenes, however, Golkar fractured between Habibie's Sulawesi/ICMI loyalists ('White Golkar') and Akbar's pragmatic Slipi party apparatus ('Black Golkar'). Recognizing that Bank Bali and East Timor had made Habibie toxic to the public and the military, Akbar quietly negotiated a vote-trading pact with Amien Rais and Gus Dur. On the night of October 19–20, 1999, dozens of Akbar's delegates defected behind the secret-ballot curtain to vote down Habibie's Accountability Speech, while Akbar secured the speakership of the DPR for himself.

In 2001, prosecutors revealed that while serving as Habibie's State Secretary in early 1999, Akbar had signed off on Rp 40 billion in off-budget poverty-relief funds from the state logistics agency (Bulog) to a shadowy foundation that whistleblowers alleged had bankrolled Golkar's 1999 campaign. Convicted of corruption and sentenced to three years in prison in 2002, Akbar refused to resign as DPR Speaker while appealing, and in February 2004 the Supreme Court controversially overturned his conviction 4–1. After losing the Golkar chairmanship to Jusuf Kalla later that year, he settled into the role of senior party patriarch, chairing Golkar's Advisory and Honorary Councils through the 2020s.

subtitle: b. 1947, Yogyakarta — Commander of ABRI/TNI & Minister of Defense (1998–1999)
desc:
Born in Yogyakarta in 1947 and raised in Surakarta, Wiranto graduated from the National Military Academy in 1968 and rose to prominence as Suharto's presidential adjutant from 1989 to 1993. Promoted rapidly through the Jakarta Garrison (Kodam Jaya), Kostrad, and Army Chief of Staff, he was appointed Commander of the Armed Forces (ABRI) in February 1998. During the May 1998 crisis, Wiranto refused calls from hardliners to crush student protesters at the parliament complex with martial force, advised Suharto to step down while pledging the military would protect the Suharto family, and promptly sidelined his chief rival, Kostrad commander Lt. Gen. Prabowo Subianto, the day after Habibie took office.

Serving concurrently as Armed Forces Commander and Minister of Defense and Security throughout Habibie's presidency, Wiranto navigated a perilous balancing act. He oversaw the fatal shootings of unarmed student protesters at Semanggi I (November 1998—where the military mobilized bamboo-spear-wielding Pam Swakarsa civilian militias) and Semanggi II (September 1999), while officers under his command armed and funded pro-integration militias in East Timor that carried out a scorched-earth campaign after the August 1999 independence ballot. At the October 1999 MPR General Session, after quietly entertaining and then declining Habibie's last-minute offer of the vice-presidential nomination, Wiranto kept the 38-seat military bloc autonomous as Habibie's speech went down to defeat.

Protected by a 2001 DPR Special Committee vote declaring that the Trisakti and Semanggi shootings were not gross human rights violations, and shielded by Jakarta from a 2003 UN-backed indictment for crimes against humanity in East Timor, Wiranto never faced trial. He founded the Hanura Party in 2006, ran for President in 2004 and Vice President in 2009, and returned to executive power under President Joko Widodo as Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal, and Security Affairs (2016–2019) and Chairman of the Presidential Advisory Council (2019–2024), before being appointed Special Advisor to the President for Political and Security Affairs by President Prabowo Subianto in 2024.

subtitle: b. 1952, Makassar, South Sulawesi — 1998 Jakarta Garrison Commander (Pangdam Jaya) & Minister of Defense
desc:
Born in Makassar, South Sulawesi, in 1952, Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin graduated from the Military Academy in 1974 in the same class as his close Kopassus associate Prabowo Subianto and spent years inside Suharto's personal presidential security detail (Paspampres). In late 1997, he was appointed Commander of Kodam Jaya, the vital military garrison directly responsible for the security of Jakarta during the collapse of the New Order.

During the May 12, 1998 Trisakti shootings and the subsequent three days of May 13–15 rioting—in which organized provocateurs torched more than 4,000 buildings, over a thousand people died in burning shopping malls, and hundreds of ethnic Chinese-Indonesian women were gang-raped—Kodam Jaya forces were conspicuously absent from key districts of the capital. On May 14, Sjafrie famously rode an armored personnel carrier through central Jakarta to calm crowds and attended the controversial meeting at Kostrad headquarters alongside Prabowo. Reassigned out of troop command after Suharto's fall, Sjafrie attributed the May security vacuum to communications breakdowns before the TGPF fact-finding team and later declined to appear under subpoena when Komnas HAM investigated the May 1998 unrest.

Because the Attorney General's Office repeatedly returned Komnas HAM's May 1998 investigative files without convening a human rights court, Sjafrie's career continued unimpeded. He served as TNI Chief Spokesperson in 2002, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Defense (2005–2010), and Deputy Minister of Defense (2010–2014) under President Yudhoyono. Brought back to the Defense Ministry as special advisor to Prabowo Subianto in 2019, Sjafrie was appointed Minister of Defense in October 2024 and awarded an honorary four-star General rank in 2025.

subtitle: b. 1940, Ketapang, West Kalimantan (d. 2024) — Chairman of PPP (1998–2007) & 9th Vice President of Indonesia (2001–2004)
desc:
Born in Ketapang, West Kalimantan, in 1940, Hamzah Haz began his career as a journalist and economics lecturer in Pontianak and rose through Nahdlatul Ulama's regional ranks before entering parliament in 1971. When the New Order forcibly merged four Islamic parties into the United Development Party (PPP) in 1973, Hamzah became a fixture on the DPR budget committee, mastering parliamentary procedure while surviving within Suharto's tightly policed opposition.

Appointed Minister of Investment in Habibie's Development Reform Cabinet in May 1998, Hamzah won the chairmanship of PPP at the party's late-1998 congress, restoring the Ka'bah as the party's symbol and Islam as its ideological foundation. Stepping down from the cabinet in May 1999 to lead PPP into the June election, he captured 58 seats in the MPR, making PPP the largest Islamic party in parliament. Though initially sympathetic to Habibie, Hamzah joined Amien Rais's Central Axis in mid-1999, voiced public reservations about a female president to block Megawati, and swung PPP's decisive bloc behind Gus Dur after Habibie's Accountability Speech was rejected.

After a brief tenure in Gus Dur's first cabinet, Hamzah became a leading parliamentary critic of Gus Dur's presidency. When the MPR removed Gus Dur in July 2001 and elevated Megawati Sukarnoputri, Hamzah promptly abandoned his earlier objections to a female head of state and defeated Akbar Tandjung and Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono in an MPR floor vote to become the ninth Vice President of Indonesia (2001–2004). He led PPP until 2007 and lived quietly in Jakarta and Bogor until his death in July 2024 at age 84.

subtitle: b. 1956, Belitung — Founder of the Crescent Star Party (PBB) & Coordinating Minister for Law and Human Rights
desc:
Born on the island of Belitung in 1956, Yusril Ihza Mahendra studied constitutional law and philosophy at the University of Indonesia and earned his doctorate in Malaysia before joining Suharto's State Secretariat as a speechwriter in the late 1990s. In May 1998, as student protesters occupied the parliament complex, it was Yusril who drafted Suharto's resignation announcement and advised B.J. Habibie on the constitutional mechanics of his immediate swearing-in at Merdeka Palace.

Two months later, in July 1998, Yusril founded the modernist Islamic Crescent Star Party (PBB), styling it as the spiritual and legal heir to the 1950s Masyumi party. Winning 13 seats in the June 1999 election, Yusril became a key constitutional strategist inside Amien Rais's Central Axis during the October 1999 MPR General Session, even standing briefly as a presidential candidate on October 20 before withdrawing at the last minute to consolidate Islamic party votes behind Gus Dur.

Renowned for his mastery of statutory law, Yusril made himself indispensable to nearly every post-Reformasi administration, serving successively as Minister of Law and Legislation under Gus Dur, Minister of Justice and Human Rights under Megawati, and State Secretary under Yudhoyono. Named a corruption suspect by the Attorney General's Office in 2008 over the Ministry of Law's online corporate registry fee system (Sisminbakum), he countersued in the Constitutional Court and had the case formally terminated via SP3 in 2012. After leading the legal defense team for Prabowo Subianto in the 2014, 2019, and 2024 presidential election disputes, Yusril was appointed Coordinating Minister for Law, Human Rights, Immigration, and Corrections in October 2024.

subtitle: b. 1941, Bandung, West Java — Coordinating Minister for Economy, Finance & Industry (1998–1999)
desc:
Born in Bandung, West Java, in 1941 into a prominent Sundanese nationalist family, Ginandjar Kartasasmita studied chemical engineering in Tokyo, joined the Indonesian Air Force (rising to the rank of Air Marshal), and entered Suharto's economic bureaucracy as head of the Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM), Minister of Mines and Energy, and head of the National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas). Unlike the orthodox US-trained 'Berkeley Mafia' economists, Ginandjar championed economic nationalism and state support for indigenous (pribumi) entrepreneurs.

On the night of May 20, 1998, meeting inside the Bappenas building as Jakarta smoldered, Ginandjar led thirteen fellow economic ministers in signing the historic letter refusing to serve in Suharto's proposed 'Reform Cabinet'—the decisive blow that forced Suharto to resign the following morning. Retained by President Habibie as Coordinating Minister for Economy, Finance, and Industry (Menko Ekuin), Ginandjar spent 1998–1999 renegotiating Letters of Intent with the IMF, overseeing the painful restructuring of Indonesia's collapsed banking sector through IBRA, and fending off opposition accusations over his past ties to Freeport mining contracts and Baligate.

Surviving the fall of Habibie's administration unscathed, Ginandjar remained a senior Golkar powerbroker in the MPR, helping steer the constitutional amendments of 1999–2002. Following the creation of Indonesia's new upper regional chamber, he was elected the first Speaker of the Regional Representative Council (DPD RI) from 2004 to 2009 and later served on President Yudhoyono's Presidential Advisory Council (Wantimpres) from 2010 to 2014.

subtitle: b. 1943, Pekalongan, Central Java (d. 2016) — Minister of Cooperatives & Champion of 'Ekonomi Kerakyatan'
desc:
Born in Pekalongan, Central Java, in 1943, Adi Sasono was a student activist at the Bandung Institute of Technology (ITB) in the 1960s before spending two decades as a community development NGO organizer and social thinker. In 1990, he helped B.J. Habibie establish the Association of Indonesian Muslim Intellectuals (ICMI), becoming its Secretary-General in 1995 and forging the bridge between Habibie's technocratic circle and urban Muslim activists.

Appointed Minister of Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises in Habibie's May 1998 cabinet, Adi Sasono became the administration's most polarizing populist figure. Championing a doctrine he called Ekonomi Kerakyatan ('People's Economy'), he pushed to dismantle ethnic Chinese conglomerate monopolies, redistribute seized BLBI forestry and plantation assets to rural cooperatives, and channel over Rp 10 trillion in subsidized central-bank credit schemes across the archipelago. While grassroots cooperatives hailed him as a Robin Hood figure, IMF officials, orthodox technocrats, and rival parties accused him of building a massive state-funded patronage network to secure Habibie's re-election in the MPR.

After Habibie's defeat in October 1999, Adi Sasono left government, briefly founded the Freedom Bull National Party (Partai Merdeka), and later returned to chair the Indonesian Dekopin cooperative council until his death in Jakarta in August 2016.

subtitle: b. 1943, Surakarta, Central Java (d. 2020) — Minister of Justice & Minister/State Secretary (1998–1999)
desc:
Born in Surakarta, Central Java, in 1943, Muladi studied law at Diponegoro University in Semarang, where he served as rector from 1994 to 1998 while sitting on the National Commission on Human Rights (Komnas HAM). Tapped by Suharto in March 1998 as Minister of Justice and retained by President Habibie in May 1998, Muladi became the primary legal workhorse of the transition cabinet, taking on the additional portfolio of Minister/State Secretary in May 1999 after Akbar Tandjung stepped down to campaign for Golkar.

Working at breakneck speed from Bina Graha and the Justice Ministry, Muladi drafted the presidential decrees releasing dozens of New Order political prisoners (including Muchtar Pakpahan and Sri Bintang Pamungkas), piloted the repeal of the 1963 Anti-Subversion Law, and steered the landmark 1999 Human Rights Act and 'One-Roof' (Satu Atap) judicial independence amendment through parliament. At the same time, as a loyal defender of Habibie and Golkar, he frequently clashed with student demonstrators and human rights NGOs over the government's handling of the Suharto corruption inquiry and the Bank Bali audit.

After leaving the cabinet in October 1999, Muladi served briefly as a Supreme Court Justice (2000–2001) and was appointed Governor of the National Resilience Institute (Lemhannas) by President Yudhoyono from 2005 to 2011, remaining an influential voice in criminal code reform until his death in Jakarta in December 2020.

subtitle: Ghalib (b. 1946, Bone; d. 2016) & Baramuli (b. 1930, Pinrang; d. 2006) — Habibie's South Sulawesi Inner Circle
desc:
Hailing from President Habibie's home province of South Sulawesi, Attorney General Lt. Gen. Andi Muhammad Ghalib (born in Bone in 1946) and Supreme Advisory Council (DPA) Chairman Arnold Achmad Baramuli (born in Pinrang in 1930) formed the core of Habibie's regional palace loyalists, nicknamed the Irama Tersedak caucus. Appointed Attorney General in June 1998 to lead the anti-KKN probe into former President Suharto, Ghalib instead saw his credibility collapse in February 1999 when the press published a wiretapped telephone conversation showing Habibie and Ghalib choreographing a deferential, pre-scripted questioning of Suharto. Four months later, anti-graft watchdogs exposed hundreds of millions of rupiah in checks from conglomerate tycoons flowing into bank accounts managed by Ghalib as head of the Indonesian Wrestling Association, forcing him to step aside in June 1999.

Simultaneously, Baramuli—a former prosecutor, provincial governor, and wealthy Golkar industrialist who headed Habibie's informal Tim Sukses re-election operation—became the central figure in the Bank Bali ('Baligate') scandal after parliamentary hearings and audits revealed he had pressured Bank Bali owner Rudy Ramli and IBRA officials over the Rp 546 billion commission paid to Golkar insiders.

Neither man ever served prison time. Military and civilian prosecutors accepted Ghalib's explanation that the tycoon payments were purely athletic donations, while acting Attorney General Ismudjoko issued an SP3 dropping the Suharto probe on October 11, 1999. Baramuli's Bank Bali indictment bogged down in court on procedural challenges until his death in 2006, while Ghalib was later appointed Indonesian Ambassador to India (2008–2009) and elected to parliament for PPP before dying in 2016 and receiving a full military burial at Kalibata Heroes Cemetery.

subtitle: Novanto (b. 1955, Bandung) & Tjandra (b. 1951, Sanggau, West Kalimantan) — Principals of the 1999 Bank Bali Scandal
desc:
Born in Bandung in 1955, Golkar deputy treasurer Setya Novanto partnered in early 1999 with Kalimantan-born property tycoon Djoko Soegiarto Tjandra (b. 1951, Sanggau) through their company PT Era Giat Prima (EGP) to extract a Rp 546 billion ($70 million) 'collection fee' from state-supervised Bank Bali—nearly 60% of the Rp 904 billion interbank claim guaranteed by Indonesian taxpayers via IBRA. When a PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) forensic audit uncovered that the funds were funneled to Golkar and Palace operators ahead of the October 1999 MPR presidential vote, the resulting 'Baligate' scandal prompted the IMF to freeze bailout disbursements and fatally crippled Habibie's re-election bid.

Both men escaped accountability for decades. In 2000, the South Jakarta District Court acquitted Djoko Tjandra on grounds that the Bank Bali cessie agreement was a civil matter, while the Attorney General's Office issued an SP3 in 2003 terminating the investigation into Setya Novanto. When the Supreme Court overturned Tjandra's acquittal on special review in June 2009 and sentenced him to two years in prison, Tjandra chartered a private jet out of Jakarta the day before the ruling and lived for eleven years as a fugitive billionaire in Papua New Guinea and Malaysia.

Unscathed by Bank Bali, Setya Novanto rose to become Chairman of the Golkar Party (2016–2017) and Speaker of the DPR (2014–2015, 2016–2017). Only in November 2017—after famously staging a car crash into a utility pole to evade KPK investigators—was he arrested and sentenced to 15 years in prison for the Rp 2.3 trillion electronic ID card (e-KTP) corruption scheme; in 2025, the Supreme Court cut his sentence to 12.5 years on judicial review, allowing him to walk free on conditional parole from Sukamiskin Prison in August 2025. Djoko Tjandra was eventually captured in Malaysia in July 2020 after a second scandal revealed he had bribed two police generals and a state prosecutor to erase his Interpol Red Notice.

term: Tim Mawar (The Kopassus Group IV Abduction Squad)
subtitle: Commanded by Maj. Bambang Kristiono (b. 1960, Purwakarta; d. 2023) with Capt. Djaka Budhi Utama (b. 1967, Jakarta) & Fellow Officers
desc:
Formed in mid-1997 inside Group IV of the Army Special Forces (Kopassus) at Cijantung under Group Commander Col. Chairawan and overall Kopassus Commander Maj. Gen. Prabowo Subianto, Tim Mawar ('Rose Team') was an eleven-man covert intelligence unit led in the field by Maj. Inf. Bambang Kristiono (born in Purwakarta in 1960). Between late 1997 and May 1998, Tim Mawar operatives abducted and interrogated more than twenty student, labor, and pro-democracy activists across Java and Sumatra; while nine activists (including Andi Arief, Desmond J. Mahesa, and Pius Lustrilanang) were eventually released alive from secret cells, thirteen others—including poet Wiji Thukul, Suyat, and Herman Hendrawan—were forcibly disappeared and never found.

When eleven Tim Mawar members were brought before High Military Court II in Jakarta in early 1999, military prosecutors restricted the indictment exclusively to the nine kidnapping victims who survived, omitting any charges regarding the thirteen missing activists or higher chain-of-command orders. In April 1999, the court convicted the officers of procedural 'insubordination,' handing down sentences of 12 to 22 months and ordering five officers dismissed from military service. None of the eleven ever served prison time: they remained on active duty while appealing to the Supreme Court, which quietly overturned their dismissals in 2007.

Every surviving officer went on to reach two-star or three-star general rank in the TNI and later entered senior civilian government roles in the 2020s: Lt. Gen. Djaka Budhi Utama (b. 1967, Jakarta) served as Inspector General of the Ministry of Defense and Principal Secretary of BIN before being appointed Director General of Customs and Excise at the Ministry of Finance in May 2025; Lt. Gen. (Ret.) Nugroho Sulistiyo Budi (b. 1967, Pekalongan) became Head of the National Cyber and Crypto Agency (BSSN) in February 2025; Maj. Gen. (Ret.) Yulius Selvanus (b. 1963, Tana Toraja) was inaugurated as Governor of North Sulawesi in February 2025; Maj. Gen. (Ret.) Dadang Hendrayudha (b. 1965, Karawang) became a senior deputy at the National Nutrition Agency in 2024; and unit commander Bambang Kristiono served as a senior Gerindra MP and Deputy Chair of DPR Commission I until his death in July 2023.

term: Sjamsul Nursalim, Anthony Salim & Bob Hasan (The BLBI Tycoons)
subtitle: Nursalim (b. 1942, Lampung), Salim (b. 1949, Kudus) & Hasan (b. 1931, Semarang; d. 2020)
desc:
During the 1997–1998 financial meltdown, Suharto's closest corporate conglomerates received over Rp 144.5 trillion in emergency Bank Indonesia liquidity support (BLBI) to cover bank runs—funds that a 2000 Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) investigation concluded were 95% diverted into affiliated group companies, currency speculation, and offshore accounts. The largest recipients were the Salim Group's Bank Central Asia, led by Anthony Salim (born in Kudus in 1949, son of New Order business patriarch Liem Sioe Liong), which absorbed Rp 52.7 trillion; Bank Dagang Negara Indonesia (BDNI), owned by tire and retail magnate Sjamsul Nursalim (born in Tanjung Karang, Lampung, in 1942), which absorbed Rp 28.4 trillion; and Bank Umum Nasional, co-owned by Suharto's golfing partner and timber monopoly kingpin Bob Hasan (born in Semarang in 1931).

While Bob Hasan was convicted in 2001 of defrauding the Ministry of Forestry's aerial mapping fund and served three years in Nusa Kambangan prison before his parole in 2004, the largest bank owners avoided prison by signing Master Settlement and Acquisition Agreements (MSAA) with IBRA in late 1998. Under those agreements, Anthony Salim and Sjamsul Nursalim surrendered corporate shares and industrial assets—later valued at a fraction of their claimed worth—in exchange for 'Release and Discharge' immunity, reinforced by formal Release Letters (SKL) issued under President Megawati in 2002–2004.

When the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) belatedly indicted former IBRA chief Syafruddin Arsyad Temenggung and Sjamsul Nursalim in 2017–2019 over a Rp 4.58 trillion state loss from BDNI's fictitious shrimp-farmer receivables, the Supreme Court acquitted Temenggung in July 2019 on grounds that the act was not criminal, and in April 2021 the KPK issued its first-ever SP3 terminating all charges against Nursalim. Bob Hasan died in Jakarta in March 2020, while Anthony Salim and Sjamsul Nursalim remain among the wealthiest billionaires in Southeast Asia, controlling vast food, mining, retail, property, and infrastructure empires across Indonesia and Singapore.

term: Eurico Guterres & Maj. Gen. Adam Damiri
subtitle: Guterres (b. 1971, Uatulari, East Timor) & Damiri (b. 1949, Garut, West Java) — 1999 East Timor Campaign Figures
desc:
Born in Uatulari, Portuguese Timor, in 1971, Eurico Guterres was orphaned during the 1970s conflict and recruited by Indonesian military intelligence into the pro-integration youth movement Gada Paksi before taking command of the Dili-based Aitarak ('Thorn') militia in early 1999. Operating alongside territorial troops under Kodam IX/Udayana Commander Maj. Gen. Adam Damiri (born in Garut, West Java, in 1949), Aitarak and allied pro-Indonesia militias waged a campaign of intimidation ahead of the August 30, 1999 UN referendum, culminating in the April 1999 massacre at Manuel Carrascalão's residence in Dili and the September 1999 scorched-earth destruction of East Timor after 78.5% of voters chose independence.

To head off a UN Security Council international tribunal, Jakarta created a domestic Ad Hoc Human Rights Court for East Timor in 2002. Of the eighteen military, police, and civilian figures tried, twelve were acquitted outright and five—including Maj. Gen. Adam Damiri and all other Indonesian military and police officers convicted—had their sentences overturned on appeal. Only Eurico Guterres, an East Timorese civilian, served two years in Sukamiskin Prison (2006–2008) before the Supreme Court vacated his conviction on judicial review in April 2008 and ordered his immediate release.

Adam Damiri retired with full military honors, while Eurico Guterres settled in Indonesia as head of the pro-Jakarta veterans' association Uni Timor Aswain (UNTAS), joined PAN and later the Gerindra Party, and in August 2021 was personally awarded the Bintang Jasa Utama—one of Indonesia's highest civilian medals of merit—at Istana Negara by President Joko Widodo.
